title: Thanksgiving Desserts 2026: Cake, Pie and More Ideas Guaranteed to Steal the Show
summary: This year, think outside the pie. Consider making a sticky miso-apple spiral, voluminous chocolate mousse with whipped cream, silky buttered corn flan and more.
body_markdown:
This year, think outside the pie. Consider making a sticky miso-apple spiral, voluminous chocolate mousse with whipped cream, silky buttered corn flan and more.


By[Genevieve Ko](https://cooking.nytimes.com/author/genevieve-ko)


Published Nov. 2, 2026


Updated Nov. 3, 2026


What if Thanksgiving dessert were something other than pie? Even if you already have dishes of[double-crust apple](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1021614-mixed-apples-pie?art=100000011239896) ,[sticky pecan](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1022734-maple-honey-pecan-pie?art=100000011239896) or[spiced pumpkin](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1023580-spiced-pumpkin-cheesecake?art=100000011239896) on the table, what if you also had tender cakes, silky custards and (surprise!) chocolate?


We already know the answer. Mixing up the sweets will make the meal only more spectacular, whether it’s a Friendsgiving party or a feast on Nov. 26. That’s why we asked seven brilliant bakers to come up with original creations that capture the spirit of the holiday, showcase the season’s harvest and surprise us with the new forms dessert can take.


Serving a variety of desserts has long been part of Thanksgiving. Pie didn’t feature prominently until the 19th century, thanks in part to Sarah Josepha Hale’s abolitionist novel[“Northwood: Or, Life North and South.”](https://play.google.com/books/reader?id=CzqzsWa1OrYC&pg=GBS.PA6&hl=en) She wrote that pumpkin pie “occupied the most distinguished niche” on the Thanksgiving table, and it then grew in popularity. But Ms. Hale also wrote about “huge” puddings and “rich cakes” at Yankee feasts, and we’re bringing that abundance to this spread.


They make a big impact on the table, but all feel light to leave you satisfied, but not stuffed. Prepare one or more of them to serve alongside (or even instead of) pie to end the meal memorably and to start delicious new traditions.

## [Dark Chocolate Mousse With Orange Whipped Cream](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/793306500-dark-chocolate-mousse-with-orange-whipped-cream?art=100000011239896)


Credit...


Christopher Testani for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Kaitlin Wayne. Prop Stylist: Megan Hedgpeth.


Credit...


Sometimes the simplest dessert makes the biggest statement, and Sue Li proves that here. She takes the chic French concept of serving a big bowl of chocolate mousse with whipped cream and eliminates the need for eggs or gelatin. Instead, an easy chocolate ganache ends up silky and rich with crème fraîche and airy with whipped cream. Folding orange zest into the cream that is piled on top uplifts it, like sun shining through fluffy clouds.


Recipe: **[Dark Chocolate Mousse With Orange Whipped Cream](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/793306500-dark-chocolate-mousse-with-orange-whipped-cream?art=100000011239896)**


## [Sweet Potato and Cranberry Layer Cake](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/793383430-sweet-potato-and-cranberry-layer-cake?art=100000011239896)


Credit...


Credit...


Well-loved classics from the savory side of Thanksgiving come together in this towering four-layer cake. Terrence Hayes sandwiches citrusy cranberry sauce between plush sweet potato cake fragrant with cinnamon and nutmeg, then slathers the tall stack with vanilla-scented meringue. Torching the meringue’s swoops and swirls not only results in a dramatic look, but it also tempers its sweetness with a welcome toastiness.


Recipe: **[Sweet Potato and Cranberry Layer Cake](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/793383430-sweet-potato-and-cranberry-layer-cake?art=100000011239896)**


## [Buttered Corn Flan](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/793382749-buttered-corn-flan?art=100000011239896)


Credit...


Credit...


Yes. A strong yes to corn in dessert. Nicola Lamb loves butter melting into warm corn on the cob and captured that marriage in this sleek, delicate flan with echoes of caramel corn. Inspired by the Mexican flan de elote, she toasts corn in butter, then infuses that into milk and cream before baking the custard over dark caramel. Because it needs to chill before serving, it can be prepared well in advance, so it’s as impressive as it is stress free.


Recipe: **[Buttered Corn Flan](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/793382749-buttered-corn-flan?art=100000011239896)**

## [Sticky Apple and Miso Spiral](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/793305712-sticky-apple-and-miso-spiral?art=100000011239896)


Credit...


Credit...


Natasha Pickowicz sketched her dream of a nostalgic apple pie with a big wow factor, then turned that drawing into this spectacular tart. Sugared-and-spiced apples are rolled into buttery sheets of phyllo. That tube is then coiled over more apples in a skillet of miso caramel. When baked, the flaky phyllo crisps on top and candies at the bottom for a deeply flavorful yet not-too-sweet pastry.


Recipe: **[Sticky Apple and Miso Spiral](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/793305712-sticky-apple-and-miso-spiral?art=100000011239896)**


## [Salted Caramel and Pecan Cream Slice](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/793384686-salted-caramel-and-pecan-cream-slice?art=100000011239896)


Credit...


Credit...


Carolina Gelen grew up in Romania eating and making cremeș, also known as cremeschnitte, krempita and cream slices. Now, she celebrates Thanksgiving stateside by giving the traditional version a hint of pecan pie. She keeps the form the same — sliceable vanilla custard sandwiched between flaky pastry — and introduces salted caramel to the filling and candied pecans on top. The scaffolds of crunchy nuts, crackly pastry and caramel cream hit every craving.


Recipe: **[Salted Caramel and Pecan Cream Slice](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/793384686-salted-caramel-and-pecan-cream-slice?art=100000011239896)**


## [Chocolate Tahini Mousse Cake](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/793370928-chocolate-tahini-mousse-cake?art=100000011239896)


Credit...


Credit...


To tie chocolate into the holiday’s flavors, this cake is topped with a maple-sweetened mousse that’s nutty with toasted sesame. Jerrelle Guy loves a little fancy in her food, and her dessert is all elegance, glossy with a ganache that envelops tender chocolate cake topped with that tahini mousse. While the taste is deep with dark chocolate, brown sugar and coffee, each bite feels light thanks to whipped mascarpone cream.


Recipe: **[Chocolate Tahini Mousse Cake](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/793370928-chocolate-tahini-mousse-cake?art=100000011239896)**

## [Persimmon Upside-Down Cakes](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/793300642-persimmon-upside-down-cakes?art=100000011239896)


Credit...


Credit...


Bright orange persimmons ripen on trees throughout the fall, and their vibrant hue and gentle vanilla-like sweetness shine in Kristina Cho’s nutty little cakes, which are sticky with toffee sauce. Thin slices of fruit pressed into the pan encase the easy batter and soften in the sauce to end up glowing like topaz. These cakes can be dressed up like a restaurant dessert and plated with whipped cream and ribbons of fresh persimmon, or just picked up and eaten by hand.


Recipe: **[Persimmon Upside-Down Cakes](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/793300642-persimmon-upside-down-cakes?art=100000011239896)**
